proposals.rationale: Hypothesis: adding the strong lithium bis(trimethylsilyl)amide base at the subsequent reaction temperature rather than at the recorded 0 °C could reduce control of the exothermic deprotonation/catalyst activation period and increase competing pathways.
Hypothesis: loss of the recorded dropwise base-addition control could create transient local excesses of strong base, with reduced selectivity or catalyst integrity.

Hypothesis: replacing the Buchwald ligand charge with an additional Pd2(dba)3 charge leaves the reaction without the specified supporting phosphine ligand, potentially producing a less active or unstable palladium catalyst system.
Hypothesis: heating without the recorded reflux condition may not sustain the intended thermal reaction regime, reducing the rate of Buchwald-Hartwig coupling.

Hypothesis: deleting the provisional reactor-to-heater connection removes the available heating-control path for the 65 °C reaction stage and may prevent attainment or maintenance of the specified temperature.
